text:
Carlos M: Quick heads-up — Orion go-live tomorrow 09:00 PT. I sketched a short customer-facing runbook for surge handling, batching, and streaming fallback. Pls review and flag anything missing.

Maya S: Love it. High-level items I want called out to the customer: priming pool size, session stickiness, and a simple retry policy. Keep it consumable.

Carlos M: Agreed. Draft excerpt for the runbook (customer-facing):
- Before go-live: open handshake window 30m prior, scale priming pool to 2x expected qps.
- Batch guidance: target 8–12 user messages per batch for chat-like flows; smaller batches (2–4) for low-latency single-turn calls.
- Streaming: use token-stream for interactive UIs; add client-side 2s idle timeout before falling back to non-streaming.
- Fallbacks: route to smaller quantized model if latency > 600ms for 3 consecutive requests.
- Telemetry hooks: surface `latency_p50/p95`, `batch_size_avg`, `stream_conn_failures`.

Ben T: Suggest adding a tiny config snippet for their frontend engineers to copy-paste. Keeps parity across teams.

Maya S: I put one together — short and explicit: 
```json
{"routing_policy":"region-first","priming_pool":50,"batch_target":10,"stream_idle_timeout_ms":2000,"fallback_policy":"quantized_small_after_3"}
```
This maps to the keys we expose in the customer console.

Alice R: Also add a renewal-risk signal checklist for CS handoffs: low weekly usage < 10k tokens, >3 config errors in 7d, or repeated latency spikes (p95 > 1s). Those trigger an enablement call.

Carlos M: Good call. I'll include a one-line customer message: "If you see latency >1s or unexpected errors, open a support ticket and we'll schedule a concierge tuning session."

Dinesh P: From the customer's POV — please include a note about sampling feedback: show 1:100 requests for manual review and expose a "flag output" button. We want an easy path to capture quality issues.

Maya S: Added. Sampling guidance: 1% random samples + deterministic sampling on new prompt templates. Also surface a short feedback form with 3 quick choices (good / wrong intent / hallucination) + free text.

Carlos M: Ops checklist for Redwood SREs (internal):
- Pre-go-live: verify priming_pool health > 95% readiness, ensure canary route ready.
- At go-live T+0..+15: monitor batch_size_avg and stream_conn_failures every 60s.
- If p95 latency climbs >20% from baseline: temporarily reduce batch_target by 25% and add extra capacity.
- If stream_conn_failures spike: fall back clients to polling (non-stream) with exponential backoff: base 250ms, max 4s.

Ben T: Small note — for the fallback text we should give a sample client message so the customer UX looks intentional, e.g.: "Experiencing intermittent stream issues — switching to a faster mode. Responses will continue as usual."

Carlos M: Perfect. I'll add that copy.

Alice R: On enablement coordination: assign an owner (CS) + SE for the first 72h, then hand to success manager. Add daily 10min stand for first 3 days to triage.

Maya S: Also recommend a short eval set (10 prompts) the customer can run post-deploy to verify behaviour. If any prompt fails the quality threshold -> escalate to model ops.

Carlos M: Cool. I'm going to paste this into the customer runbook doc and share the public link in the morning. If no objections, I'll create the support template and the feedback sampling rules. :thumbsup:

Ben T: No objections from infra. I'll be oncall T+0..+48.

Alice R: I'll own enablement handoff. Sending calendar invites now.

onboard-bot: Reminder scheduled: "Orion go-live prep" at 08:15 PT tomorrow for channel / customer kickoff.

Carlos M: Thanks everyone — saved. If anyone wants to add short copy for the customer-facing UX messages, drop it here and I'll fold it in.
